scenario: Synthetic Single filer with $15,000 W-2 wages below the $15,750 standard deduction — zero taxable income and childless EIC

reconciliation.scope: Targeted arithmetic correction, not full source/eligibility certification.
basis: Historical issue-77 review was a targeted arithmetic correction only; it did not certify source documents, eligibility, or a completed IRS return.
Case-specific authority and synthetic assumptions are recorded in provenance. This case has no qualified dividends or capital gains, senior deduction, qualifying children, or child-credit claim.

assumptions: Closed-world synthetic return: a Single employee born March 15, 1990, with one W-2, $15,000 wages, $0 federal withholding, and no other income, adjustments, itemized deductions, estimated payments, or credits except the childless EIC.

Filer is under 65, not blind, not another person's dependent or qualifying child, resident in the United States for more than half the year and an all-year tax resident, with a timely employment-valid SSN and no prior nonclerical EIC disallowance. Eligibility review references in input.json are synthetic declarations, not taxpayer or IRS records.

Earned income and AGI are both $15,000; investment income is zero; there are no qualifying children or other dependents. Childless EIC eligibility is assumed under Publication 596 (2025), pp. 2–6 and its rules for filers without a qualifying child.
No business, self-employment, REIT, PTP, qualified-dividend, capital-gain, foreign-exclusion, income-averaging, kiddie-tax, or other special-tax activity exists.

No dependent-care expenses or benefits, education source documents, eligible education expenses, Marketplace coverage, advance premium credits, policy allocations, or premium-tax-credit activity exists. No fake empty Form 8863 or student record is supplied.

The sole employer reports $15,000 Social Security and Medicare wages, $930 Social Security withholding and $218 Medicare withholding. There is no excess Social Security withholding, Additional Medicare Tax withholding, or other employment-tax adjustment.
All $312 of overpayment is requested as a refund, with none applied to the following year's estimated tax and no other refund elections or adjustments.
limitations: This is not an IRS-published full-return example. Only the $15,750 deduction and $312 EIC are directly published amounts; other expectations apply IRS instructions to synthetic facts or the explicitly identified benchmark balance/intermediate convention. None were generated by the engine or a calculator.
A synthetic benchmark pass and citation presence do not certify actual eligibility, source authenticity, a completed IRS return, PDF or MeF correctness, or filing readiness.

Zero-activity assertions establish no contribution from a successfully recorded producer or an explicit optional-without-source inactive producer. They do not assert hidden worksheet values; absent, failed, unavailable, or unrecorded execution cannot establish zero.

Positive combined CTC/other-dependent or AOTC/LLC contributions cannot be disaggregated into these zero-only component assertions. Multiple candidate contributions are ambiguous rather than silently summed.

ordinary_taxable is an ordinary-route parsed calculation input, not a separately filed Form 1040 line. Preferential, foreign-exclusion, income-averaging and special-tax routes are outside this assertion's supported scope.
The October 14 issue-77 review remains historical targeted arithmetic work, not retrospective full source or eligibility certification.

line9_total_income.basis: p. 1, lines 1a, 1z and 9: the sole $15,000 W-2 wage amount and no other income yield $15,000 total income.

line11_agi.basis: p. 1, lines 9–11a: $15,000 total income minus no adjustments yields $15,000 AGI.

standard_deduction.basis: p. 6, standard deduction: the 2025 Single amount is $15,750; the synthetic filer is under 65, not blind and cannot be claimed as a dependent.

qbi_deduction.basis: p. 1, lines 1–15: no qualifying business, REIT or PTP income is assumed; assert no Form 8995 contribution to Form 1040 line 13a, not a private worksheet value.

line15_taxable_income.basis: p. 2, lines 12e–15: $15,000 AGI less $15,750 deduction and no QBI deduction is negative; line 15 instructs entry of zero.

ordinary_taxable.basis: p. 68, Tax Table zero-taxable-income row, applied after Form 1040 line 15's zero floor: this benchmark names the ordinary-rate calculation input $0, not a filed line or an IRS-published worksheet intermediate. No preferential or special route is assumed.

income_tax.basis: p. 68, Tax Table $0–under-$5 row, Single column: $0 taxable income yields $0 ordinary income tax; no special line-16 taxes apply.

se_tax.basis: pp. 1 and 4, who must file and income subject to self-employment tax: ordinary employee W-2 wages are not self-employment earnings. Assert no Schedule SE contribution to Schedule 2 line 4.

add_medicare_tax.basis: p. 1, lines 1–7: $15,000 Medicare wages are below the Single $200,000 threshold, with no other covered wages or self-employment activity. Assert no Form 8959 contribution to Schedule 2 line 11.

line18_tax_before_credits.basis: p. 2, lines 16–18: $0 income tax plus no Schedule 2 line 3 taxes yields $0 tax before credits.

nonref_ctc.basis: p. 1, Part I: no qualifying children or other dependents means no Schedule 8812 contribution to Form 1040 line 19. This zero-only assertion does not disaggregate positive CTC and other-dependent credits.

dependent_care_credit.basis: p. 115, Schedule 3 line 2 instructions: no qualifying persons or dependent-care expenses are assumed; assert no Form 2441 contribution to Schedule 3 line 2.

aotc_nonref.basis: pp. 1–2, Parts II and III: no education source or qualified expenses exist, so assert no Form 8863 contribution to Schedule 3 line 3. Explicit optional inactive evidence is permitted; nonexistent trace is not. Positive combined AOTC/LLC is not a component oracle.

aotc_refundable.basis: pp. 1–2, Part I line 8 and Part III: no education source or qualified expenses exist, so assert no Form 8863 contribution to Form 1040 line 29. No invented student facts or fake empty Form 8863 are used.

ptc_additional.basis: p. 1, lines 24–26: with no Marketplace coverage, premium tax credit, advance credits or allocations, assert no Form 8962 contribution to Schedule 3 line 9.

ptc_repayment.basis: p. 1, lines 27–29: no advance premium tax credit payments exist, so assert no Form 8962 repayment contribution to Schedule 2 line 1a.

eitc.basis: p. 31, 2025 EIC Table: at least $15,000 but less than $15,050, Single with no qualifying children, gives $312. Both earned income and AGI are $15,000; eligibility remains an explicit synthetic assumption under pp. 2–6 and the childless eligibility rules.

actc.basis: p. 2, Part II: no qualifying children means no additional child tax credit; assert no Schedule 8812 contribution to Form 1040 line 28.

excess_ss_credit.basis: p. 117, Schedule 3 line 11 instructions: the sole employer withheld $930 on $15,000 Social Security wages, with no multi-employer excess. Assert no W-2 producer contribution to Schedule 3 line 11.

line24_total_tax.basis: p. 2, lines 18–24: $0 tax before credits, no nonrefundable credits, and no other taxes yield $0 total tax.

line33_total_payments.basis: p. 2, lines 25–33: no withholding or estimated payments plus the $312 EIC and no other refundable credits yields $312 total payments.

line35a_refund.basis: p. 2, lines 34–36: $312 payments minus $0 total tax gives $312 overpayment; all is requested as refund and none applied to next year.

line37_amount_owed.basis: p. 2, lines 34–37: payments exceed tax, so there is no balance due. The existing benchmark's numeric balance convention records the non-applicable owed side as $0; this does not claim that a filed form must print a zero.
